title: Kernel flavor sensitivity labbook — INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ mixtures
content:
Summary:

Quick labbook capturing a set of microbenchmarks and mixed-workload runs exploring sensitivity of our kernel implementations to: INT8/GPTQ/AWQ and FP8 representations, tile sizes, and vector-lane packing. Goal: surface reproducible performance/quality tradeoffs and short actionable mitigations for tail-latency and throughput regressions we saw in the last canary. This is intentionally informal — raw numbers, hypotheses, and next steps.

Hardware + runtime snapshot:
- HW: p4d.24xlarge equivalent V100->A100-like profile (40GB), mixed cluster nodes for some runs (A100-80GB for long-context).
- Driver: nvidia-driver 525.xx, CUDA 11.8.
- Runtime: redwood-serving v0.78.1 (sha: a7f4d3c).
- Profilers: CUPTI + nvprof for kernel-level timelines, nv-nsight for a couple deep traces, custom microprof harness (bench-client v2.3).

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Models: small: Llama-7B-quant (GPTQ), medium: Falcon-7B (FP32 baseline), large: Red7B-AWQ (experiment AWQ).
- Quant formats: GPTQ(8-bit per-channel), AWQ(8-bit asymmetric), INT8 symmetric baseline, FP8 e5m2 variant for comparison.
- Kernel flavors: baseline (tile=128x32), packed-vector (tile=64x64, vector lanes enabled), fused-gemm (kernel fusion enabled), streaming (reduced scratch memory, copy-avoid).
- Workloads: short-chat (avg len 40 tokens), long-context (avg len 1024 tokens), bursty-mix (90% short, 10% long).
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec (throughput), GPU occupancy, sustained SM utilization, L2 bandwidth, memory stalls, validation loss delta and perplexity on small eval set to estimate quality drift.

Representative commands used:
- microbench: ./bench-client --model red7b-awq --format awq --kernel packed-vector --threads 8 --warmup 200 --runs 2000
- long-context replay: ./replay-driver --trace traces/long/2025-03-01.json --model llama7b-gptq --kernel fused-gemm

Key raw observations (numbers are median of 3 runs unless noted):
1) Packed-vector kernel (tile=64x64) + AWQ on Red7B: +18% tokens/sec vs baseline tile, but p99 latency regressed on long-context by ~27ms. GPU traces show bursts of L2 serialization when KV cache writes happen. Hypothesis: packed-vector increases L2 write amplification due to smaller tile strides for KV writeback.

2) GPTQ model (per-channel INT8) using fused-gemm kernel: throughput ~3.1k tokens/sec for short-chat, p90 stable. However for bursty-mix p99 spikes correlate with dispatcher contention (thread sleeping/waking). Flame graphs show CPU spin waiting for work-queue with 18% CPU time in futex/epoll.

3) FP8 variant produced slightly higher quality (perplexity down 0.9%) vs INT8 on eval set, but runtime overhead adds ~6% latency at kernel launch due to extra conversion code path (not fused). When FP8 codepath was fused with the main matmul kernel (proto-fusion), the overhead disappears and we get 4% throughput improvement over INT8 in some inputs (surprising — likely lower quantization-induced compute because of better alignment).

4) AWQ artifacts: certain AWQ packing patterns expose an instruction divergence in warp-lane writes on A100 with vector-lane enabled. Observed in Nsight: up to 12% warp idle time during KV writes on long sequences.

5) Cold-starts: models with larger per-layer scratch (fused-gemm) show a ~60–120ms cold-start penalty due to cudamalloc/cudaFree fragmentation. Using a preallocated mempool reduced cold-start by ~80ms and improved p99 by ~10% for first requests.

Profiling snippets / signals worth noting:
- L2 bandwidth utilization often saturates before SM; kernels that increase scatter/writes suffer on long contexts.
- High kernel launch overhead when codepath branches per-block (FP8 conversion path not-inlined).
- Dispatcher contention is visible in our client harness under bursty arrival patterns: reduce runtime thread context switches by increasing batch-capacity or using lightweight fibers.

Quality checks:
- Small eval: 250 prompts derived from SQuAD-like Q/A + 50 synthetic instruction prompts. Measured average log-likelihood delta vs FP32 baseline. AWQ and GPTQ show small delta (<2% LL change) for short-chat, but for long-context AWQ had 3–6% LL degradation for a subset of prompts with repeating patterns (likely quantization noise accumulation in KV cache).

Hypotheses / Root causes (ranked):
A) L2 write amplification from tight tile packing + KV writes -> throughput gains short, tail degradation long.
B) Codepath branching for FP8 and AWQ -> kernel-launch overheads and warp divergence.
C) Host-side dispatcher queueing -> p99 latency spikes under bursty mix.
D) Memory allocation overheads for fused kernels -> cold start penalties.

Quick mitigations tested (and results):
- Increase tile stride for KV write path only (hybrid tile): reduced p99 long-context by ~20ms, sacrificing 6% tokens/sec on short-chat.
- Inline FP8 conversion into main kernel (proto-fusion): removed ~5–8% kernel-launch overhead, throughput improved ~4% for mixed workloads.
- Enable mempool with reuse for fused kernels: cut cold-start by 80ms and reduced p99 by ~10% on first-window traffic.
- Dispatcher: changed to lock-free queue (experiment code): reduced CPU wait stalls, p99 improved 12ms in bursty-mix.

Unresolved anomalies (to investigate):
- Occasional 2–3x p99 spikes under AWQ with packed-vector on one node type only (A100-40GB vs 80GB). Hypothesis: micro-architectural buffer sizes differ and amplify writeback serialization. Need reproducible minimal trace.
- Some prompts with repeating tokens show progressive quality degradation in AWQ but not GPTQ — could be related to asymmetric quantization bias.

Next experiments (concrete):
1) Minimal reproducer for AWQ packed-vector p99 spike: isolate KV write kernel + synthetic pattern, run Nsight timeline. Owner: Evan. Target: 2025-04-07.
2) FP8 fused kernel cleanup: land prototype fusion in runtime branch and run 50-run smoke across model catalog. Owner: Priya. Target: 2025-04-10.
3) Dispatcher A/B: compare lock-free queue and current implementation under traffic generator for 24h to check stability. Owner: Luis. Target: 2025-04-12.
4) Quantization quality test: design longer-sequence synthetic suite (repeat patterns, adversarial prompts) to stress AWQ accumulation. Owner: Maya. Target: 2025-04-09.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Save full Nsight traces for cases (1) and (5) to "/traces/awq/packed-vector/2025-03-31/".
- Postmortem template: capture trace id, kernel name, small repro script, hardware id.
- Add a small script to toggle mempool via env var for quick canaries.

Decisions (tentative):
- For canary next week, disable packed-vector kernel for AWQ models on long-context routing (fallback to baseline tile). Risk: small throughput loss but reduces observed p99 regressions.
- Prioritize FP8 fusion work — if fusion yields both quality and perf wins, we can consider it for medium models.

Appendix (small table of representative numbers, short-chat workload):
- Baseline tile (int8): throughput 2.45k tps, p50 12ms, p99 62ms, eval delta 0.0
- Packed-vector (awq): throughput 2.89k tps (+18%), p50 10.5ms, p99 89ms (+43%), eval delta +3.2% LL
- Fused-gemm (gptq): throughput 3.10k tps (+26%), p50 9.8ms, p99 65ms, eval delta +1.1% LL
- FP8-fused (fp8 fused): throughput 2.59k tps (+5.7% vs int8), p50 11ms, p99 60ms, eval delta -0.9% LL

If anything here looks questionable or you want the raw traces/bench outputs, I can attach the zipped traces and the bench-client logs (they're big).
